ai.description: The Beaked Worm Snake reaches 60 cm. It is uniform brown or grey above with a paler underside. A prominent, sharp, beak-like rostral scale distinguishes this burrowing, blind-eyed species.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Beaked Worm Snake is best identified by its prominent, sharply pointed, and beak-like snout, which distinguishes it from the rounded heads of other Indian blind snakes.
ai.habitat: The Beaked Worm Snake inhabits moist, deciduous forests and agricultural areas across peninsular India, typically burrowing in loose soil from sea level to 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Beaked Worm Snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, using its pointed, hardened snout to burrow through soil in search of earthworms and insect larvae.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Grypotyphlops acutus* is oviparous, laying clutches of 2–8 elongated eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Beaked Worm Snake occurs across peninsular India, ranging from the Gangetic plains south to Kerala, typically inhabiting lowlands and elevations up to 1,500 meters.
